text.p: **BIRTHDAYS**
Pioneer Queensland bush balladist ALEXANDER FORBES was born in 1839. He wrote "Voices From The Bush".
Australian author WILLIAM ASTLEY was born in 1855. He collected and wrote history books and Australiana.
American entertainer and sharpshooter ANNIE OAKLEY was born in 1860. She could shoot coins and cards out of the air, and reportedly once shot a cigarette out of the mouth of Kaiser WILHELM.

The founder of the Australian Communist Party, JOHN 'JOCK' GARDEN, was born in 1882. The colourful Scots-Australian clergyman was charged with inciting unionists to murder, and also with fortune telling. He was acquitted on both counts.

The inventor of television, Scotsman JOHN LOGIE BAIRD, was born in 1888. In 1925 he used a tea chest, knitting needles, a bike lamp, a cake tin, string and sealing wax to create his first television set. The first image transmitted was that of a ventriloquist's dummy.
British film director ALFRED HITCHCOCK was born in 1899. His thrillers included "Psycho", "Rear Window" and "The Birds".
American actor JOHN DEREK was born in 1926. His wife MARY COLLINS became known as the "Perfect 10", BO DEREK.
Cuban revolutionary leader FIDEL CASTRO was born in 1927. He became socialist president in 1959.
British singer and bass player with The Batchelors SEAN JAMES STOKES was born in 1940.
British bassist and singer with Paper Lace CLIFF FISH was born in 1949.
American singer, guitarist, pianist and songwriter DAN FOGELBERG was born in 1951. He was a great musician on records by JACKSON BROWNE, VAN MORRISON and RANDY NEWMAN.

British singer FEARGAL SHARKEY was born in 1958. He was leadsinger of the Undertones from 1981 until they split up in 1983. After a brief time with VINCE CLARK in Assembly FEARGAL SHARKEY went solo. His hits include "A Good Heart" (1985) and
"You Little Thief" (1986).
**EVENTS**
1521 : HERNANDO CORTES, Spanish conqueror, captured and
destroyed Tenochtitlan (Mexico City) after a three month siege. 1587 : The first American Indian to convert to
Christianity in the English colonies was baptised in the Church of England. His name was MANTEO.
1814 : The Cape of Good Hope was formally ceded to the
British by the Dutch.
1844 : Explorer Dr LUDWIG LEICHHARDT and his party set
out on their expedition between Brisbane's Moreton Bay and Port Essington.
1852 : British politician BENJAMIN DISRAELI wrote "These
wretched colonies will all be independent in a short time, and are a millstone round our necks."
1910 : British nursing pioneer FLORENCE NIGHTINGALE died.
In 1856 she had founded the Nightingale School and Home for Nurses in London.
1912 : The cost of living inquiry in Sydney was told that
Australian mutton was cheaper in London than on the local market.
1914 : France declared war on Austria-Hungary, leading to
World War One.
1940 : Four Australian war leaders were killed when an

RAAF bomber crashed. The four were among ten people who died when the bomber came down in the hills near Canberra. Chief of the General Staff Sir BRUDENELL WHITE, the Minister of the Army, Brigadier G.A. STREET, the Minister of Air, J.V. FAIRBAIRN and the Vice-President of the Executive Council, Sir HENRY GULLET, were killed. The four had come from Melbourne to attend a Cabinet meeting.
1946 : British author H.G. (HERBERT GEORGE) WELLS died.
He wrote many short stories, but was best known for "War Of The Worlds" (1898).
1961 : The border between East and West Berlin was closed
at the Brandenburg Gate, heralding the construction of the Berlin Wall.
1962 : On the first anniversary of the Berlin border
closure, East German PETER FECHTER, was shot while trying to escape to the West.
1964 : The last hangings in Britain took place when two
men were executed for murder at Liverpool and Manchester.
1966 : In Melbourne, 29 people died when fire swept
through the Salvation Army's men's hostel.
1969 : As relations worsen between China and the Soviet
Union, the two sides accuse each other of sending troops across the border at Sinkiang and inflicting heavy casualties.
1978 : A bomb ripped through the Beirut headquarters of
AL-FATAH, the rivals of the Palestine Liberation Front. More than 150 people were killed.
1989 : Thirteen people were killed when two hot air

balloons collided near Alice Springs in the Northern Territory. The tragedy happened about 10 minutes after four hot air balloons carrying tourists has taken off. The collision was Australia's worst hot air balloon accident, with one of the balloons plunging 182 metres to the ground.
1991 : Britain's new Dangerous Dogs Act came into force.

Fighting dogs such as the pit bull terrier and tosa had to be muzzled and leashed in public. Owners who failed to comply could be fined almost $4,000 and jailed for six months. The legislation followed a series of dog attacks, in particular the near-fatal pit bull attack of a six-year-old child, three months earlier.
1994 : Under an agreement with the U.S., North Korea
agrees to freeze its graphite-moderated nuclear power programme in favour of systems less capable of producing weapons-grade plutonium.
1996 : Data sent back by the Galileo space probe
indicated there may be water on one of Jupiter's moons, heightening the possibility it could support a primitive life form.
